analysis:
This batch holds only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/glm-openrouter-returned-reasoning.md, lines 1-7) and a 5-line addition plus a date bump in docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines ~874-878). No executable source is in scope, so no code-level security regression can be established here.

The documented behavior changes are in GLM-5.3-Flash request handling. Strict tools are now accepted and each auto tool call is validated against its schema before exposure, instead of constraining decoding. Earlier-turn reasoning (`reasoning` or `reasoning_details` text) is rendered as `reasoning_content` in template history. Empty-string tool arguments are read as `{}`. Null reasoning members are treated as unset, and the `thinking` switch is accepted as a Boolean or an object.

The changelog says contradictory switches, unknown reasoning members, `preserve_thinking`, forced tool choices and hidden reasoning are still refused. That fail-closed posture is described as unchanged.

Open questions for any pass that sees the code (GLM5NextPromptPolicy.RawControls, `returnedReasoning`, ToolConstraintValidation.validate):
1. Consumer-supplied assistant-turn reasoning is injected into the prompt. This is prompt input from the consumer to the provider and carries no new trust-boundary crossing (A-001), but rendering should not allow template-control injection or break the shipped-template SHA check.
2. Validation of `strict` tool calls must fail the request on a non-conforming call and must not leak the raw output (T-007, T-008).
3. Relaxing null and empty handling must not weaken the refusal of exclude/hidden reasoning.

None of this can be verified from the supplied documentation, so I record these as unverified contracts rather than findings. The change does not touch the cache, attestation, key or coordinator-protocol threats (T-041, TB-011).
